title: AI Just Helped Find Two New Superconductors
hook: Machine learning helped physicists find two new superconductors and sketch a faster route toward physics' biggest prize in the field: a superconductor that works at room temperature.

title: Mass vs. Weight
hook: Your mass is the same on the Moon as on Earth — but your weight isn't. They're related, but they are not the same thing.

title: The Sun Says No to the Higgsino Explanation
hook: If a Higgsino caused LZ's odd recoil, the Sun would have been quietly hoovering up dark matter for billions of years — and IceCube would see the neutrinos. It doesn't.

title: Turning Cosmic Rays Into Random Numbers
hook: Muons rain down from the sky in unpredictable directions. Point a telescope at them and you have a physical random number generator — one useful for closing a loophole in Bell tests.

title: Precision Quantum Simulation of Magnon Spectra and Interactions
hook: A 97-qubit quantum processor just simulated the spin-wave ripples inside a magnet more precisely than any classical computer can — a real step toward quantum computers helping discover new materials.

title: NASA's Roman Telescope Is Cleared to Launch
hook: Hubble sees deep; Roman is built to see wide. NASA has cleared its next flagship observatory for a late-August launch to map cosmic expansion across huge swathes of sky.

title: Swift Is Working Again, and Falling
hook: NASA has revived two of Swift's telescopes after a failed commercial reboost attempt. The problem now is not electronics but air: atmospheric drag is pulling the observatory down faster than expected.

title: Inside the Atom
hook: An atom is almost entirely empty space wrapped around a tiny, dense nucleus — and the number of protons in that nucleus is what makes an atom gold instead of oxygen.

title: Entanglement Made From Plain Sunlight
hook: Quantum entanglement was thought to need a laser's disciplined light. An outdoor experiment made it from raw sunlight instead.

title: Closing the Last Loophole in a Fiber-Based Bell Test
hook: Time-bin entanglement is how quantum signals travel down real optical fiber — but the standard measurement quietly throws away photons. This test finally plugs that hole.

title: Quantum-Classical Crossover in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Dynamics Simulation
hook: A new paper puts an actual number on 'when do quantum computers win': about 2 hours and 370,000 qubits to beat 100 years of classical computing on one benchmark physics problem.

title: A Supernova That Peeled Back a Star's Layers
hook: A rare supernova exposed material from one of the deepest layers of a dying star — a direct look inside the element factory hidden in massive stars.

title: Spacetime From Entanglement — and 'Magic'
hook: If quantum entanglement weaves space-time together, what makes it bend into gravity? Theorists now point to a stranger ingredient they call 'magic.'

title: CERN Wants to Drop Atoms Down a Shaft
hook: A 100-metre vertical atom interferometer in an LHC access shaft would hunt ultralight dark matter in a mass range nothing else can reach — and listen for gravitational waves below LIGO's floor.

title: Using Wobbling Starlight to Find Dark Matter Clumps
hook: A passing dark matter clump would nudge the Earth, and that nudge would tilt every star's apparent position at once. TESS has the sky coverage to look for that shared tilt.

title: A 'Black Hole Star' in the Early Universe
hook: JWST found something from the universe's first few hundred million years that looks like a giant star but shines a hundred billion times too brightly to be one.

title: Diamond, Crushed Past Neptune's Pressures
hook: Squeeze diamond harder than the inside of Neptune and it stops behaving the way theory predicted — new experiments finally settled a 20-year argument between calculation and measurement.

title: Why Everything Falls at the Same Rate
hook: Drop a hammer and a feather together in a vacuum and they hit the ground at the same instant. Gravity doesn't care how heavy you are — and that fact runs surprisingly deep.

title: Evidence for Sequential Υ(nS) Suppression in Light Ion Collisions
hook: Physicists just found the same 'melting pattern' that signals a quark-gluon plasma — the universe's primordial soup — in much smaller particle collisions than ever confirmed before.

title: Static Electricity and Lightning
hook: The shock from a doorknob and a bolt of lightning are the same thing at wildly different scales: charge that piled up with nowhere to go, suddenly leaping across a gap.

title: A Bell Test on Where Atoms Are Going
hook: Bell's inequality has fallen for photons and atomic spins. Now for motion itself — entangled helium atoms that defy local realism about their own momentum.

title: The muon puzzle: air showers make more muons than physics predicts
hook: Cosmic rays hitting the atmosphere produce far more muons than any collider-tuned model expects. Auger now says the fix is that proton collisions must dump several times more energy into hadrons.

title: Tiny Magnetic Waves Could Shrink Quantum Computers to Coin Size
hook: Magnons — quantum ripples of magnetism once too short-lived to use — just got a 100x lifespan boost, and the bottleneck turns out to be manufacturing, not physics.

title: Why Orbits Are Ellipses, Geometrically
hook: Newton's inverse-square law implies planets trace conic sections. Most proofs are a calculus slog — this one finds a constant ratio hiding in the velocity and lets geometry finish the job.

title: Atmospheric Pressure
hook: Air has weight, and the whole column of it above you presses down — about 101 kPa at sea level. That push is what makes straws and suction cups work.

title: How Orbits Work: Falling and Missing the Ground
hook: A satellite in orbit is falling the whole time — it just moves sideways so fast that the Earth keeps curving away beneath it.

title: Two Ways a Monster Star Dies — and Only One Makes a Mess
hook: Stars of thousands to tens of thousands of solar masses collapse straight to black holes. Numerical relativity shows the lighter ones leave far more debris behind — and can still explode.

title: Quantum Entanglement
hook: Two particles can share one quantum state so tightly that measuring one instantly fixes the other's matching property — even light-years apart. Einstein called it spooky.

title: How Rainbows Form
hook: A rainbow isn't an object in the sky — it's sunlight bending through millions of raindrops, each splitting white light into colors and bouncing one back toward your eyes.

title: Sensitivity Is Only a Third of What a Quantum Sensor Owes You
hook: Two quantum magnetometers with identical headline sensitivity can disagree about the field by a factor of nearly 200. A new framework says which physical mechanism is to blame for which failure.

title: Could We Ever Tell a Gravitational Wave Is Quantum?
hook: If gravity is quantum, gravitational waves should arrive in squeezed quantum states. This analysis finds nearly every route to observing that squeezing quietly destroys it.

title: The Photoelectric Effect
hook: Shine the wrong color of light on a metal and nothing happens, no matter how bright. Switch to a bluer color and electrons fly off instantly. That puzzle proved light comes in packets.

title: 390 Gravitational Waves In, and Black Hole Astronomy Is Just Getting Started
hook: The latest gravitational-wave catalog leaps to 390 confirmed detections — including the clearest signal ever caught and evidence some black holes are built from earlier mergers.

title: Gyroscopes: Why Spinning Things Stay Upright
hook: A spinning top won't fall over and a rolling coin stays balanced. Spin gives an object a stubborn sense of direction — angular momentum resists any attempt to tip its axis.

title: Physicists Made a Quantum System's Arrow of Time Run Backward
hook: By carefully steering quantum measurements, researchers made a system behave as if time were flowing in reverse — and found they could harvest energy from the trick itself.

title: An Electric Field Trick That Nearly Triples Heat Flow
hook: Zap a ceramic crystal with an electric field and heat suddenly flows through it almost three times faster in one direction — a jump far beyond anything researchers expected.

title: The H₀ World Cup II: A Comprehensive Competition Between Proposed Hubble Tension Solutions
hook: Fourteen rival theories all claim to fix cosmology's biggest headache — the Hubble tension. A new 'World Cup' pits them head-to-head on the same data to see which ones actually survive.

title: Testing Hawking's Area Law on 241 Mergers
hook: Black-hole horizons can never shrink — a theorem checked so far on a handful of loud events. Sorting a whole catalogue into first- and second-generation black holes turns it into a population test.

title: A Chemistry Question Solved Without a Quantum Computer
hook: Many assumed only a quantum computer could crack certain chemistry problems. A result decades in the making shows an ordinary computer can do it after all.

title: Why That Eclipse Looked Golden
hook: Spain's total solar eclipse showed a gold corona instead of the usual pearly white. The Sun wasn't different — the air in front of it was.

title: What Is a Wave?
hook: A wave moves energy from place to place without moving the stuff it travels through — the water bobs, but the wave races on.

title: How Much Quantum Magic Lives in the Correlations?
hook: Magic is the resource that makes a quantum computer hard to simulate. A new result pins down exactly how much of it hides in the correlations between two parties rather than in each one's local basis.

title: Heat vs. Temperature
hook: A sparkler can hit thousands of degrees yet barely burn you — because temperature and heat are not the same thing.

title: James Webb Reveals a Strange Atmosphere on a Hellish Lava Planet
hook: A planet so hot its surface is an ocean of molten rock turns out to have a real atmosphere — built from gases venting straight out of the lava itself, JWST finds.

title: Listening for Moonquakes to Find the Moon's Hidden Ice
hook: Buried lunar ice can't be seen from orbit — but it changes how seismic waves bend and bounce, so a moonquake could map it for you.

title: A Maser Shrunk Onto a Chip
hook: Masers are lasers for microwaves: exquisitely quiet, ideal for hearing faint signals, and stuck inside bulky metal resonators. This one runs at room temperature on a chip.

title: In General Relativity, Not Everything Falls the Same Way
hook: Galileo's rule — all objects fall alike — holds for points, not for shapes. In general relativity a body's lumpiness accelerates it, and two identical starts can diverge.

title: Ordinary WiFi Can Recognise You Through a Wall
hook: The radio waves already bouncing around your flat carry a shape — yours. Researchers turned unencrypted WiFi chatter into an image good enough to identify 197 people almost perfectly.

title: A Single Laser Shot Now Images Through 15 Meters of Lead
hook: Muon imaging usually means waiting hours for enough cosmic-ray muons to trickle through. A laser-driven muon beam just did the same job — through a truck and a building wall — in a single shot.

title: A Nuclear Reactor Still Glows After You Switch It Off
hook: Shut a reactor down and the fission stops — but the fuel keeps emitting antineutrinos for months. Physicists have now caught that ghostly afterglow for the first time.

title: The universe's most energetic particles come from nearby
hook: Match the sky map of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays against catalogues of galaxies and the signal snaps into focus at one distance: everything within about 60 megaparsecs.

title: Giant Black Hole Seeds May Be Far Easier to Make Than We Thought
hook: To grow the monster quasars seen in the early universe, you need heavy black hole seeds — and those were thought to require rare, intense radiation. New simulations say a modest glow will do.

title: The Magnetic Bubble That Saved Jupiter's Moons
hook: Jupiter has four giant moons. Saturn has essentially one. New simulations pin the difference on a magnetic bubble that kept young Jupiter's moons from spiraling to their deaths.

title: Can Classical Probability Alone Explain the Double-Slit Pattern?
hook: The double-slit interference pattern is physics' go-to symbol of quantum weirdness. A theoretical study shows classical probability alone can reproduce it, given the right ingredients.

title: Watching a Heavy Object Harder to Make It More Quantum
hook: Decoherence erases quantum behaviour in anything massive. A proposal turns the quantum Zeno effect around: repeated measurements pile up their own disturbance until the weirdness is visible.

title: Nuclear Fission
hook: Split one heavy nucleus and it releases neutrons that split more — a chain reaction that, tamed, lights cities, and unleashed, levels them.
